payload.author: exam:1@run-140
payload.body:
examiner (run-140 task 1): writing `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_fold_policy.mjs` against M1–M8.

Approach: copy `test_run_engine_ready_set.mjs`'s shape (its `drive`/`taskOf`/`waitUntil`/`readEvents`/`kernelSeam` helpers) rather than importing it, pass `foldAgeMs` through `extraArgs`, and register every run in a `RUNS` array that leg (a)'s sweep reads.

Scenario map:
- (a) sweep over every RUNS entry: `why` in {released,end,aged} on every `driver:wave-adopted`/`driver:wave-blocked`; the released-ids check (each id dispatched after the event with `head === e.headSha`) applied to **adopted** events only — run-136 reviewer finding (2), since a blocked epoch carries no `headSha`.
- (b) M2 threshold: three staggered no-edge landings (stagger ~400 ms, `check.sh` sleeps 0.2 s so the baseline wall is ~200 ms) with `foldAgeMs` absent / `'x'` → one epoch `why:'end'` (proves the threshold is max(60000, wall) and not the wall); with `foldAgeMs: 0` → first epoch `why:'aged'`.
- (c) M3: same three, `foldAgeMs: 600000` → one epoch `['X','Y','Z']` `why:'end'`; `foldAgeMs: 0` → >=2 epochs, first `why:'aged'`.
- (d) M4: A→C, B→C, `foldAgeMs: 600000` → epoch 1 `['A','B']` `why:'released'` `released:['C']`, C started after it on that `headSha`, epoch 2 `['C']` `why:'end'`; plus the aged pair (A at once, B held 2 s, `foldAgeMs: 300`).
- (e) M5: in that aged pair, the adoption's `ts` within one second of A's `worker:end` + 300 ms, and the adoption before B's `worker:end` — the lane woke on its own timer.
- (f) M6: CONTRACT.md read over the fourth `Run:` line's own sed range, same regex.
- (g) M7: the three sibling sims read **as text** (`fs.readFileSync` only — never `existsSync`/`statSync` and never a spawn, which is what `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs`'s sibling rule and its leg (e) actually forbid). The three `Run:` lines carry the rest.
- (h) M8: `foldAgeMs: 0` + an exec-seam hold on the kernel's first `fold` until Y and Z have returned → exactly two adoptions, `['X']` then `['Y','Z']`; plus the same three with no hold, each task in exactly one epoch.

Expected red at BASE: `why` is absent from every event, so leg (a) fails first.

payload.author: impl:1@run-140
payload.body: Approach for task 1 (fold policy). The trigger goes into `claimEpoch` as a predicate over the ready-set state, computed by a new `foldTrigger()` defined beside `isReady`/`takeReady` (nothing calls either until the lanes run, so definition order is free): `released` first (a queued task whose every predecessor is adopted or among the pending results), then `end` (nothing in flight, nothing folding, nothing ready), then `aged` (oldest pending result's `landedAt` vs the threshold). A claim stops being a bare array and becomes `{ results, why, released? }` — `foldPending`/`foldEpoch` destructure it, and both `driver:wave-adopted` and `driver:wave-blocked` gain `why` (and `released` when that is the trigger). The red-baseline park's blocked event carries the triggering `why` too, defaulting to `end` at the run's tail, so every wave event of every run names one of the three. Threshold: `args.foldAgeMs` when finite and >= 0, else `Math.max(60000, baselineWallMs)` where the wall is measured around the baseline `sh(testCmd, baselineDir)` and recorded in `settleBaseline`; `null` (clause off) until it settles. M5's wake is a race in the lane between `nextLanding()` and an unref'd timer at `threshold - age(oldest)`, cleared by whichever side wins. The lane keeps BASE's order (claim, then takeReady, then the quiet test), which already folds a pending set before the run is judged quiet.

payload.author: exam:1@run-140
payload.body:
Exam written: `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_fold_policy.mjs`. Red at BASE for one reason — the fold policy does not exist, so every landing folds and no event carries `why`. First failure is leg (b)`s `foldAgeMs`-absent run: 3 adoptions where 1 is owed.

Readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. **`why` precedence is deliberately not pinned.** With `foldAgeMs: 0` at a run`s LAST landing, both `aged` and `end` hold, and the task does not say which wins. So every `why` this exam asserts by value comes from a scenario where exactly ONE clause can have fired: b1/b3/c1 assert `end` at a last landing under a threshold nothing can age into; b2/c2 assert `aged` at a FIRST landing while two workers are still in flight (so `end` is false); d1 asserts `released` at B`s landing (A alone released nothing) and `end` at C`s; d2 asserts `aged` on a 300 ms threshold while B is held 2 s. h1/h2 use `foldAgeMs: 0` and assert only `tasks`, never `why` — the sweep checks membership in the set and no more. An implementer is free to order the three clauses any way.

2. **Leg (a)`s released-ids check is asked of `driver:wave-adopted` only** (run-136 reviewer finding 2) — a blocked epoch has no `headSha` to dispatch a released task on. The sweep also records, per run, that no scenario here folds a red epoch, so that scoping is visible rather than assumed.

3. **`released` on a non-released epoch** is asserted absent-or-empty, not strictly absent — both spellings say the same thing and pinning one picks an implementation.

4. **Leg (g) reads the three sibling sims as TEXT and never runs them.** `fs.readFileSync` of a sibling`s path is not an offender under `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs`: its `sibling` rule is scoped to SPAWN call sites, and its leg (e) to `existsSync`/`statSync`/`accessSync`. Verified — the hermetic probe sweeps 28 sims with this file present and names 0 offenders.

5. **Leg (g) accepts BOTH shapes of the ready-set edit.** For each of the eight tags it accepts `foldAgeMs: 0` inside that scenario`s own block OR inside that sim`s `drive` helper where the helper names `c1` as the exception — the task`s Context reads either way. `c1``s own block is required NOT to carry it. The scenario slice runs from `tag: ` <id> `` to whichever of the next tag or the next column-0 `}` comes first; checked against BASE, every slice lands inside its own block.

6. **Leg (e)`s timing budget is measured, not guessed.** Fold latency from `worker:end impl:A` to the adoption event in this rig at BASE is 307–349 ms over three probe runs with the default fast `check.sh`. With a 300 ms threshold the aged adoption is owed at ~640 ms against a 1300 ms ceiling, and B is held 2000 ms — so a lane that only wakes on a landing misses by a second. The `sleep 0.2` `check.sh` is used ONLY by leg (b)`s three runs, where a ~200 ms baseline wall is the whole point of `max(60000, baselineWallMs)`; putting it in the aged run pushed fold latency to 568 ms and made the window tight, which is why it is not there.

7. **Leg (h) is expected GREEN at BASE** — it is run-136`s deleted `c1` pin carried forward, and BASE already partitions a mid-fold landing correctly. It goes red only through the leg (a) sweep`s `why` check. That is intended, not a gap.

Legs (b)(c)(d)(e)(f)(g) and the (a) sweep are red at BASE; every "sim precondition" assertion passes, so no failure reads as a typo, a bad import or a missing fixture. Nothing under `unsatisfiable`.

payload.author: impl:1@run-140
payload.body:
Landed as 6626621a. Decisions a later session would otherwise rediscover:

- Trigger precedence is released -> end -> aged, evaluated in `foldTrigger()` next to the readiness helpers (it reads that state). The first that holds is the `why`, so a fold that releases is named for the release even when the run happens to end with it. With `foldAgeMs: 0` the first landing of an edgeless run reads `aged`, not `end` — workers are still in flight.
- `claimEpoch()` now returns `{results, why, released?}` instead of a bare array; `foldEpoch(claim)` spreads the trigger onto both `driver:wave-adopted` and `driver:wave-blocked`.
- `parkOnRedBaseline(why = "end")` takes the claim`s trigger so that EVERY wave event carries a `why` in {released,end,aged} — including the red-baseline park, which has no claim behind it at the run`s tail.
- `nextLandingOrAge()` falls back to plain `nextLanding()` when `epochClaimed`. Without that guard, `foldAgeMs: 0` with results pending during another lane`s fold arms a 0 ms timer and hot-spins the lane for the whole fold. Those results belong to the epoch after the running fold anyway, and the fold`s own release announces.
- `foldAgeMs` is a FUNCTION, not a value: the default arm depends on `baselineWallMs`, which is null until the baseline settles. A null threshold is the age clause off, not a guessed number — `released` and `end` carry the run until the suite has answered.
- `r.landedAt` is stamped in `settleResult` BEFORE the claim, so a result the same turn`s claim takes folds at age zero.
- `releasedBy` guards on reusedIds/dispatchedIds/resultFor/blockedByDep as well as !isReady, so a reused or already-failed task never counts as released.
- Sim placement: `foldAgeMs: 0` is written literally inside each of the eight ready_set scenarios that are not about the trigger (not centralised in `drive`), so a text-reading exam leg sees it per scenario. In test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs there are FOUR rig sites, not one — the `fixture()` helper, ub1, ub2, and the embedded probe template string; ub2`s three-epoch pacer precondition fails if you only patch the helper.
